title: Cricket from First Principles — Journalism Story Map
purpose: Map Study 21 questions to real cricket evidence so the article demonstrates the analysis rather than listing conclusions.

questions.study_question: What does it mean to win?
questions.analytical_point: A result depends on the format and the match state, not on runs alone.
Runs are the basic scoring unit, but a score has meaning only inside the state of the match.

questions.study_question: What limits the accumulation of runs?
questions.analytical_point: Runs are accumulated while wickets, deliveries and/or playing time are being consumed.

questions.study_question: Why do wickets matter beyond changing the score?
questions.analytical_point: A wicket can become the scarce resource that ends a chase even when many runs remain.
No. Their value can depend on who faces them and what state follows.

questions.study_question: How does a fixed number of deliveries change the problem?
questions.analytical_point: In limited-overs cricket, each legal delivery consumes a finite resource.

questions.study_question: How can time itself change what a side is trying to do?
questions.analytical_point: In a Test, consuming time can become more valuable than scoring runs when a draw is the attainable result.

questions.study_question: Does the value of runs, wickets, deliveries and time stay fixed?
questions.analytical_point: No. Their value changes with match state.
Tactics change probabilities; execution and chance still determine what actually happens.

questions.study_question: What is the fielding side trading off?
questions.analytical_point: Run prevention and wicket-taking can pull in different directions.

questions.study_question: What does a field setting represent?
questions.analytical_point: A field setting allocates limited fielding resources across space.

evidence.label: MCC/ICC result rules
evidence.job: Establish formal result conditions without turning the article into a rules explainer.

evidence.label: MCC scoring rules
evidence.job: Establish runs as the basic score.

evidence.label: Test / ODI / T20 format constraints
evidence.job: Show that different formats constrain scoring with different combinations of wickets, deliveries and time.

evidence.label: Headingley 2019 — Stokes and Leach
evidence.job: Show that remaining deliveries are not equivalent because both sides care who faces them; also show state-dependent run value and the wicket/run-prevention trade-off.

evidence.label: Sydney 2021 — Australia v India
evidence.job: Show time becoming the scarce resource and the batting objective shifting from chasing runs to surviving.

evidence.label: 2016 World T20 final
evidence.job: Show a fixed number of deliveries as an explicit disappearing resource.

guardrails: Do not turn Headingley into a detailed captaincy or optimal-field analysis.
Use real examples to answer Study 21 questions; do not write question -> answer -> proved.
The glossary handles vocabulary; the article must still explain ideas that matter to the argument.
Not every Study 21 question needs a full scene. Some should be established briefly.
Field placement is a bridge to the later spatial studies, not the destination of this article.
